blocks.text: Goes here. Principles and philosophies for growing an organic audience, relying on word-of-mouth rather than algorithms, deciding when to quit or push through a "dip," and the overall mindset required to build a brand organically.
why: Explains Seth Godin's foundational marketing philosophy—that marketing is creating the conditions for an idea to spread, rather than hustling to interrupt people with average products.
topics: [organic marketing, word-of-mouth, the dip, authenticity vs consistency, remarkable products]

Topics. organic strategy / defining marketing as "creating the conditions for an idea to spread," relying on word-of-mouth over algorithmic hacks; product design / the necessity of being "remarkable" (worth making a remark about) rather than just pushing average products to average people; consistency / "authenticity is for amateurs, consistency is for professionals," the requirement to deliver on the brand promise regardless of personal feelings; the dip / knowing when to quit early versus pushing through the hardest part of the journey.

The "Remarkable" Benchmark: A product is only remarkable if it is literally worth making a remark about. If a product doesn't naturally trigger a conversation (like TOMS shoes vs. TOMS coffee), word-of-mouth will fail.
Authenticity vs. Consistency: The concept that customers do not want your "authentic" bad day; they want the consistent version of you that you promised them.

The Dip: The philosophy of identifying the hardest point of a journey before you start. If you do not have the resources or stamina to survive the dip, do not start the project. Quit early, not in the middle.
Skip. Podcast promotional intros, sponsor reads for Storyblocks or Jotform, or general banter about the host's agency.
Scope mix. 100% baseline (philosophical foundations of marketing).
